title: Market Positioning Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 11
description:
Mrs. Rao stands in front of a shelf full of snacks: biscuits, sweets, chips and protein bars. Why should she pick Laddoo Lab? She has about two seconds to decide. In this animated lesson we use Laddoo Lab, a millet laddoo brand from Bengaluru, to understand market positioning.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definition of a product's position and where the word came from (Al Ries and Jack Trout, Positioning: The Battle for Your Mind, 1981). Then watch Zoya draw a positioning map live, place cream biscuits, sweet shop mithai and protein bars on it, and find the empty spot: healthy, and made for tiffins. That becomes Laddoo Lab's position, the healthy sweet for tiffin boxes. We fill in Kotler and Armstrong's positioning statement template, test which differences are worth shouting about, and see four positioning angles at work today, in a phone maker, an airline, a bank and a bakery. We also look at the human side honestly: a clear position makes choosing easy, but a position is a promise, and too many claims lead to confused positioning.

This is Episode 11 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
